objectives.text: Name the roots, stem and leaves, say what each part does, and trace water on its journey from the roots up the stem to the leaves
successCriteria: I can say the roots hold the plant in place and drink up water and minerals from the soil
I can trace one drop of water from the roots up the stem to the leaves and say the leaves use it with sunlight to make food
assessmentPoints: Part-naming answers in the opening activity
Water-journey tracing in the second and third activities

objectives.text: Explain why plants do not take food from the soil, and what the roots really take from the soil
successCriteria: I can explain that the roots drink water and minerals only and are not a mouth
I can explain that the leaves make the food with sunlight, so the plant does not eat food like we do
assessmentPoints: Trap discussion in the fourth activity
Worksheet and exit ticket answers in the closing practice

activities.title: Roots: the plant holds on and drinks
Stem: the plant's lift and road
Leaves: the plant makes its own food

differentiation.support: Provide a simple roots-stem-leaves diagram with arrows so learners can follow one drop of water from the soil to the leaves before tracing it themselves.

activities.title: A common mistake: plants do not eat food from the soil

differentiation.stretch: Ask learners to explain why the drinking roots prove the plant does not eat food from the soil like we eat through our mouths.
